newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Kohl, Klaus sign Czech-German accord.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Klaus sign Czech-German accord.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Tuesday signed a joint declaration meant to cement post-war reconciliation between Germany and the Czech Republic.

In the accord, Bonn expresses its sorrow at the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of Czech lands and Prague its regret at the post-war expulsion of some 2.5 million Sudeten Germans. Germany also backs Czech membership of the European Union and NATO.
"The declaration which we have just signed is a big step forward for both of our nations," Kohl said after the signing in Prague's Liechtenstein Palace.
"We cannot stay in the past or in the end the past will win," Kohl said, adding that the accord would mean better neighbourly relations and peaceful co-existence in Europe.
Klaus said in his speech that Czech-German relations had never been better.
"I am convinced that today's visit to Prague heralds a new stage in relations between our countries," he said.
The two countries also agreed to set up a 160 million mark ($100 million) "Future Fund", mainly with German money and intended primarily to benefit victims of Nazi aggression.
The accord, drawn up after two years of delicate talks, is controversial in both countries. Czech far-right Republicans and communists oppose it.

Opponents of the accord staged a small but noisy demonstration, which was disrupted by the head of the Czech police, Oldrich Tomasek, unplugging a microphone being used by Republican Party chairman Miroslav Sladek.
